feedback.answered: The removal history completed in both option modes. Without step-down, node 1 retained StateLeader and voters=[2] after applying removal at index 4, then emitted ReadState index 4 after node 2 elected itself and applied a new value at index 6. With step-down, node 1 was leaderless follower and emitted no ReadState. Source inspection distinguishes this cardinality-only shortcut from the normal read acknowledgement path. The two-node configuration is discouraged for availability, not prohibited by S_MEMBERSHIP_DOC; neither participant fails in this history.

This is a local read-certification concern; the documented application wait and caller retirement policy bound any claim of an externally served stale read.

grounding.derivation: S_READ_SAFE_EXPECTATION attributes safe read certification to communication with the quorum. S_SINGLETON_EXPECTATION describes the communication-free case specifically as a single voting member that is the leader. Taken together, that local self-certification is qualified by local identity, not merely a cardinality-one configuration. This is a derived local implementation responsibility, not a claim that all removed-node API calls are forbidden or every emitted ReadState directly completes a linearizable application read. A singleton configuration whose sole voter is another node provides no local quorum support to the responding instance. The implementation observation that the predicate omits identity motivates checking the relation but does not supply the normative expectation.
grounding.applicability: S_REMOVAL_OPTION documents optional removal step-down without stating that false disables ReadOnlySafe. RawNode.ReadIndex has no removal precondition and RawNode has no lifecycle Stop API; caller retirement remains an explicit excluded deployment policy. The actual history activates removal through committed entry application, without illegal ApplyConfChange injection. ReadState emission, not subsequent application read, is the selected endpoint.
alternatives: StepDownOnRemoval=true prevents this path by changing role; that is a valid protection and a separate control.
External caller retirement prevents reachability but does not change the conditional responsibility for this explicitly live instance.
The documented application-progress condition limits broader consequences and is not silently replaced by an assumed application read.
